vulnerability.title: Symfony Process resolves cmd.exe through the current working directory on Windows, allowing a planted cmd.exe to hijack command execution

fixed_releases.verified_content: At v5.4.46 prepareWindowsCommandLine() resolves cmd.exe with ExecutableFinder and uses the absolute path; v5.4.45 hard-codes the bare name "cmd"

fix_commits.message: [Process] Use %PATH% before %CD% to load the shell on Windows

severity.numeric_level_rationale: The CNA record published by GitHub_M scores the issue 0.0 None, while the GHSA/OSV data labels it HIGH with a CVSS 3.1 8.4 vector (AV:L/C:H/I:H/A:H) and NVD Primary scores 9.8 Critical with AV:N. The canonical severity keeps the CNA vector verbatim and records all three; the 0.0 is an upstream inconsistency, not a judgement that the issue is harmless. The dataset treats the GHSA High and NVD Critical scores as published values and does not adopt either as fact.
severity.source: GitHub_M CNA CVSS 3.1 metric (0.0 NONE); GHSA/OSV label HIGH with CVSS 3.1 8.4; NVD Primary 3.1 9.8 CRITICAL
severity.ghsa_label_note: GHSA and OSV label the issue HIGH; the CNA CVSS field is 0.0 NONE with an all-zero impact vector. NVD independently scores 9.8 Critical and switches the attack vector to network. The three published assessments are irreconcilable; no single score is canonical in practice, so the CNA value is kept for schema stability and the others are recorded.

vulnerability.category_l2: Windows shell resolution / binary planting: bare cmd.exe resolved through the current working directory

critical_operation.description: prepareWindowsCommandLine() builds the command line for every Windows process as the literal string "cmd /V:ON /E:ON /D /C (...)". The shell name is not resolved through an absolute path or through %COMSPEC%; Windows resolves a bare "cmd" against the current working directory before (or ahead of) the system directory in the search order used here. If an attacker can place an executable cmd.exe (or cmd.bat/cmd.cmd, depending on PATHEXT) in the working directory of the PHP process, that binary is launched instead of the system shell and receives the full command line, which is command-execution hijacking. The 5.4.46 fix resolves cmd.exe with ExecutableFinder (which prefers PATH) and quotes the absolute path. The issue is Windows-specific; on Unix-like platforms prepareWindowsCommandLine() is not called.

entry_point.description: An application runs a Process on Windows with a working directory that an attacker can write to (uploads, extracted archives, shared temp dirs).

trace.description: prepareWindowsCommandLine() hard-codes the bare shell name "cmd"

location.verification_method: Static read of Process.php at v5.4.45 and v5.4.46 plus the fix patch and ancestry; no process was started and no binary was planted.

source_crosscheck.notes: All sources agree on CWE-77, the Windows cmd.exe resolution defect, the <5.4.46 range and fix 18ecd03e. Severity is irreconcilable: CNA 3.1 0.0 None, GHSA/OSV HIGH (8.4), NVD Primary 3.1 9.8 Critical with AV:N.

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read Process::prepareWindowsCommandLine() at v5.4.45 and confirm the bare "cmd" invocation and that it runs on Windows.
An independent reviewer must confirm 18ecd03e is absent from v5.4.45 and present in v5.4.46, and that it resolves cmd.exe through ExecutableFinder.
An independent reviewer must assess the CNA 0.0 versus GHSA High versus NVD 9.8 discrepancy and the Windows-only applicability.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
Windows-only vulnerability; the snapshot is platform-independent but no Windows execution was performed and no cmd.exe was planted.
The CNA score is 0.0 None while GHSA/OSV label the issue High and NVD scores 9.8 Critical; the dataset records all three and does not resolve the contradiction.
Only the 5.4 branch was inspected; 6.4.14 and 7.1.7 were not diffed.
Whether the attacker-controlled working directory is reachable depends on the application; no specific deployment was analysed.
open_questions: The exact Windows binary search order (CWD versus System32) for the bare name was not tested.
Whether all Process use on Windows passes through prepareWindowsCommandLine() was not exhaustively audited.
